_about: Full-episode-only keys for scenarios/awareness_e19_malware_and_updates/scenario.json.erb (the E19 consequence-flip episode). The Sonnet wiring agent pastes each value into the full erb at the path its _notes line gives. None of these is in the fragment-erb parity comparison (episode-level, or allow-listed erb-only), and the generated defend-only shell never carries them. Authored by opus48. ENG-04 (the mistake stage, flip.mode montage and the flipMontageByChoice allow-list entry) and ENG-09b (conceptPanel array) and ENG-08 (schema) must have landed first. E19 is a consequence flip, so there is NO attack block, NO phish target, NO osint/write/mfa stage, NO flipAftermath, NO stepLabels, NO playerSentAuth: the mistake sandbox is the one 'attack artefact'.

_notes.mistake: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.mistake (ENG-04). The four everyday choices across the afternoon, unscored, one safe option per beat (the awareness.rb lint requires exactly one safe:true per beat, and approvedRoute must be the safe one). flipBeat is restart_prompt (aw2's one consequential choice, quoted back as the montage headline; the montage still shows every beat). A defendOnly shell must NOT carry this block (mistake_checks errors), which is why it lives here, not in defend.json.
_notes.flip: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.flip (ENG-04). mode is 'montage', the only mode; with a mistake block present the flip replays the sandbox as a calm montage. A defendOnly shell must NOT carry this block either.
_notes.flipMontageByChoice: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.flipMontageByChoice in the FULL erb only. Erb-only (STRINGS_ERB_ONLY_OK, added by ENG-04); on the parity allow-list (ENG-09d). Keyed beat then option; a line is authored for BOTH options of every beat, so ENG-04's unsafe-option fallback never fires for E19. The montage shows the line for the option the learner actually took, and the engine renders its own 'Your call' / 'Your call: the safe route' tag (flip-view.js), so the authored lines are plain sentences with no 'Your choice.' prefix (dropped 2026-10-29 to stop duplicating the engine tag, as E11 and E15 did). flipHeading ('Later that afternoon') is NOT here: it stays in defend.json strings (E19 spec section 10), shared by both shells.
_notes.conceptPanel: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.conceptPanel (ENG-09b array form) in the full erb. IDENTICAL to the value in e19/defend.json awarenessEpisode.strings.conceptPanel: the generator carries that into the defend-only shell too, so all four cards show in both variants (E19 spec section 12). Reproduced here only so the full erb's strings block carries the array. conceptPanel is value-exempt and erb-only-OK in the parity allow-list, so no allow-list change is needed.

beats.situation: Your Quayholt laptop, mid-afternoon: "Updates are ready. Restart to finish installing them. Postponed 3 times."

options.label: Save your work and restart now, or schedule it for tonight and leave the laptop on

beats.situation: A credit-note document you weren't expecting opens blurred behind a yellow bar: "Macros have been disabled. Enable content to view."

options.label: Click Enable content to read it

beats.situation: Quayholt Protect pops up: "Threat blocked: a file tried to run. Action needed." It keeps reappearing and the work feels slow.

options.label: Leave protection on and tell the service desk what it found

beats.situation: The claims spreadsheet you've been working on all afternoon is sitting on your desktop; it's needed on Monday.

options.label: Move it to the team drive

restart_prompt.postpone_again: At a quarter to four, ransomware swept the floor, and the machines that had never restarted were the ones it locked. The fix that would have shut the door it used came out last month.
restart_prompt.restart_or_schedule: The version where you postponed it again: the machine that had missed last month's fix was the one the ransomware locked at a quarter to four. The ones that had restarted held.

enable_content.enable_it: The credit note had nothing to show. The moment you enabled it, a hidden program ran with your access and reached the shared drive you reach. Quayholt Protect caught this one, but it doesn't catch every one.
enable_content.report_dont_enable: The version where you enabled it: a hidden program would have run as you, reaching whatever you can reach. Reporting it and leaving it shut left nothing to clean up.

security_alert.allow_it: Allowing it let a hidden program run, quietly, one built to copy your saved passwords. Nothing looked wrong that afternoon; days later your saved password was used to sign in from a place you have never been.
security_alert.keep_on_report: The version where you turned it off: a hidden program would have run unseen and copied your saved passwords. Leaving protection on and telling the service desk got the file blocked for everyone.

save_location.leave_on_desktop: The file on the desktop was locked with everything else, and the desktop isn't backed up. The team spent Saturday rebuilding it by hand.
save_location.move_to_drive: The version where you left it on the desktop: it was locked with everything else, and the desktop isn't backed up. On the team drive it was restored by Monday.

conceptPanel.heading: It runs with your access
conceptPanel.text: A program, a macro inside a document, or an app you connect, runs with your access. It can read what you can read, send as you, and reach the shared drives you reach. That's why a file or an app you weren't expecting is worth stopping for, even a familiar-looking one.

conceptPanel.heading: Updates close known holes
conceptPanel.text: Most updates fix a hole attackers already know about. When your device or IT asks, install it and restart the same day; many only finish after a restart. A web page offering you an update is a different thing, and never genuine (E10).

conceptPanel.heading: Ransomware, and what you do
conceptPanel.text: You might see files that won't open or have strange names, or a message that your files are locked with a demand to pay. Report it straight away. Don't pay, don't contact the attackers, don't try to fix it; if the team asks, disconnect from the network and leave the device switched on.

conceptPanel.heading: Allow this app?
conceptPanel.text: A link or an app asking to read your mail or your files is asking for your access without a password. Only approve something you, or IT, set up and trust. If you didn't start it, deny it and report it.
